title: Simplified Technical English for operator-consumed artifacts
summary: Every durable artifact an operator reads MUST be written in the Simplified Technical English baseline adapted from ASD-STE100 Issue 9 and referenced by this policy.
instructions: Agents writing an artifact an operator reads MUST read the complete Simplified Technical English guidance this policy references, and MUST apply it before completion. Governed artifacts are operator briefs, workflow-stage narratives, intake, plan, review, QA, investigation, repair, and ship records, pull-request descriptions, release notes, changelog entries, and the operator-facing summary in a stage output.

Machine records, invocation and delegation cards, JSON state, source code, code comments, commit messages, and repository documentation under docs/, README.md, and governance/ are outside the writing rules of this policy, and agents MUST NOT restyle them to satisfy those rules.

Agents MUST apply the durable-instruction-text rules in the referenced guidance to every instruction surface, including AGENTS.md, policies, criteria, skills, personas, and commands. Instruction text MUST state the rule a reader needs and MUST NOT record the request that produced it, the rejected alternative, or the reasoning that produced the wording.

Agents MUST hold instructions to a maximum of 20 words per sentence and explanation to a maximum of 25 words per sentence, counted by the referenced counting rules rather than by raw whitespace tokens. Identifiers, file paths, commands, inline code spans, quoted text, headings, numbers with units, abbreviations, and hyphenated words each count as one word.

Agents MUST write instructions in the imperative form and active voice, MUST limit a paragraph to one topic and six sentences, and MUST NOT use a semicolon, a contraction, a Latin abbreviation, a progressive or perfect tense, or an -ing form outside a domain term.
Agents MUST use one term for one concept and MUST prefer the term the repository already established in AGENTS.md, the target-repo primer, or the brief semantic registry over a new synonym.
Agents MUST preserve quoted text, captured command output, and preserved evidence verbatim. Rewriting evidence to satisfy a writing rule is an evidence defect and MUST NOT occur.
Operator chat reports MUST state the outcome, consequence, and next action. They MUST use plain language and avoid unnecessary workflow mechanics.
Operator chat reports MUST follow the referenced sentence and paragraph limits.
Operator chat reports SHOULD use simple, concise, action-oriented language.
Agents MUST NOT write dense chat paragraphs that include all context. The operator can request more detail.
Operator chat reports MUST NOT use LLM-native jargon.
Operator chat reports MUST NOT use journalistic hooks or delay a conclusion.

When an agent reports an issue, the report MUST state the issue concisely, existing consequences, anticipated consequences, and applied remediations. The report MUST give mitigation options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation.
An outcome summary MUST list key outcomes and outstanding items. Each outstanding item MUST list action options and identify whether an agent, the operator, or either can act.
When one operator-owned path resolves an outstanding item, the report MUST provide numbered steps. Each command MUST use a fenced code block and include exact parameters.
Chat-report issue and outcome shapes MUST remain judgment-only. The deterministic check does not test these shapes.

This policy adopts Part 1 writing rules of ASD-STE100 and does not adopt the Part 2 controlled dictionary as a gate. Agents MUST NOT describe an artifact as conformant to ASD-STE100, because full conformance requires the dictionary.
Agents MAY use RFC 2119 requirement keywords in governance-bearing prose, because those keywords are terms of art in this repository rather than ordinary wording.
The deterministic check MUST pass for final PR descriptions and remains advisory for other operator artifacts.

The deterministic check bound to this policy covers only the countable rules and is advisory. Agents MUST NOT treat a passing check as conformance, and a review gate MUST evaluate terminology consistency, noun-group length, voice, and risk-notice correctness by judgment.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you write an artifact that an operator reads.
